extracted.intended_audience: Small business applicants to NIH SBIR/STTR (resubmitting unfunded applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting a resubmission of an unfunded NIH Small Business (Seed/SBIR/STTR) application, including what to include in the one-page Introduction, procedural form/field requirements, timing limits, and recommended interactions with Program Officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: A resubmission is an unfunded application that has been modified in response to the initial review and has been resubmitted for consideration. In a resubmission you can provide additional information which is intended to address reviewer concerns and improve your score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmissions differ from initial applications because they respond to reviewer feedback; however, the process for resubmitting is exactly the same as for the first submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-page Introduction attachment (Response to Reviewer Comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmissions include a one-page Introduction attachment where you can summarize additions, deletions, and changes to the application following the initial review and resulting feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Introduction is an important communication with reviewers. It is recommended (but not required) you: thank the reviewers for their thoughtful comments; directly address the issues and concerns raised in the summary statement; and summarize substantial additions, deletions, and changes you are making to the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not mark up specific changes within application attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not mark up specific changes within application attachments (e.g., do not highlight, color, bold, or italicize changes); simply summarize the changes in the Introduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inline visual edits in attachment PDFs—use the one-page Introduction to explain what changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmissions may include substantial changes to application body
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmissions can include substantial changes to the body of the application (e.g., research strategy, human subjects, project team, budget, etc.) and are not limited to changes made in response to reviewer feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may revise major elements of the project; ensure substantive revisions remain within the NOFO and opportunity-specific constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to standard page limits and opportunity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Your resubmission must follow the standard page limits and other requirements of the opportunity used for the resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when making substantial changes, do not exceed the page limits or deviate from formatting/attachment rules specified by the NOFO or application system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission channels and general process
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmission applications must be submitted through Grants.gov to NIH using ASSIST, Workspace, or an institutional system-to-system solution following the same process as your original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the same electronic submission route as the original application; follow system instructions for attachments and metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: NOFO must allow resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmission must be listed in the Application Types Allowed section of the notice of funding opportunity (NOFO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the specific NOFO you are targeting permits resubmissions before preparing and submitting one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide prior application identifiers on SF424 R&R
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the Institute or Center code and serial number from your initial application in the Federal Identifier field (box 4a) on the SF424 R&R form (e.g., CA987654 from 1R42CA987654-01 A0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurately include prior application identifiers so administrators and reviewers can link the resubmission to the original summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select 'Resubmission' in Type of Application field
rubrics_metrics.description: Select 'Resubmission' in the Type of Application field (box 8) on the SF424 R&R form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the application type is correctly indicated on the SF424 R&R so the submission is processed as a resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and one-time limit for resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: You only have 37 months after your initial application to resubmit, and you only have one opportunity to resubmit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because only one resubmission is allowed, carefully consider whether resubmission or submitting a new application is the better strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult the NIH Program Official before resubmitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up a phone consultation with your Program Official (PO); this PO is listed at the top of the Summary Statement for the Institute or Center to which your application was assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared in the PO conversation to discuss: whether the reviewer comments seem 'addressable'; how you are prepared to address the reviewer's comments; and how to fit your most important responses to the reviewer's comments into one page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer as a reviewer to learn the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: The best way to learn about the review process, including what reviewers are looking for, is to volunteer to be a reviewer. The Center for Scientific Review (CSR) is always looking for new peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volunteering can improve understanding of reviewer expectations and improve future applications; consider signing up if eligible.
